title: Indian startups raised $2.2B in Q3 2026 as deal count fell 13%
excerpt: Indian startups raised $2.2B in July-September 2026, up 5% YoY per Inc42, as deals fell 13%. AI led sectors; Tracxn puts 2026 funding so far at $10.3B.
content:
Indian startups raised $2.2 billion between July and September 2026, 5% more than the $2.1 billion raised in the same quarter of 2025, according to Inc42's Q3 2026 funding report. The money went to fewer companies: the number of deals fell 13% year on year to 210, as investors wrote larger cheques to a smaller set of startups.

The year-to-date picture looks similar. Data platform Tracxn puts Indian tech funding for January to September 2026 at $10.3 billion, up 7%, even though the number of funding rounds fell 38%, according to its India Tech 9M 2026 report.

The quarter in numbers

These figures are from Inc42's report, published on 30 September:

  • Total funding: $2.2 billion, up 5% from $2.1 billion in Q3 2025.
  • Deals: 210, down from 240 a year earlier.
  • Mega rounds (at least $100 million): four, against one in Q3 2025.
  • Median deal size: $3 million, unchanged from a year earlier.
  • Active investors: 511 unique investors, down 24% from 676.
  • New unicorns (startups valued at $1 billion or more): two, Emergent and Astrotalk, against none a year earlier.

Each tracker counts deals in its own way, so the totals differ. Entrackr recorded $2.9 billion across 266 transactions in Q3, up from $2.78 billion a year earlier. By its count, though, funding has slowed every quarter this year, from $3.87 billion in Q1 to $3.5 billion in Q2.

The biggest rounds

In Inc42's data, the quarter's largest round went to Emergent, an AI platform for building apps without writing code. It raised $130 million from investors including Creaegis, Khosla Ventures, SoftBank, Lightspeed and Y Combinator, and became a unicorn. Electric scooter maker River raised $120 million. Fintech company Navi raised $100 million from Prosus, and spacetech startup Pixxel raised $100 million from a group that included Temasek and 360 ONE Asset.

Entrackr ranks the rounds differently. EV maker Simple Energy tops its list at $182 million, followed by SiMa.ai at $150 million and then Emergent. Entrackr also counts a $100 million round for fintech Slice. You can follow new rounds as they are announced on our funding tracker.

Sectors: AI moves to the top

According to Inc42, AI was the most-funded sector, with $438 million across 35 deals, up 265% from a year earlier. Emergent's round alone made up close to 30% of that total. Cleantech came next with $433 million across 23 deals, about three times last year's figure, and deeptech raised $290 million, up 176%.

Consumer sectors cooled. Ecommerce funding fell 31% to $245 million across 44 deals, and fintech slipped 11% to $249 million across 13 deals. Entrackr's sector totals differ, with $635.3 million for AI and $583 million for EV startups, but it also ranks AI first.

Series A and B carried the quarter

Inc42 found that growth-stage rounds (Series A and B) drew $1.1 billion across 90 deals, up 38% year on year. Late-stage funding (Series C and beyond) fell 10% to $994 million across 27 deals. Seed funding fell 18% to $164 million across 93 deals.

The pattern suggests investors are backing companies that already have traction rather than taking early bets. Location concentrated too. Bengaluru startups raised more than $1.4 billion across 80 deals, or 64% of all funding in the quarter.

January to September: $10.3 billion, according to Tracxn

Tracxn's nine-month report covers 1 January to 21 September 2026. It puts total funding at $10.3 billion, up from $9.7 billion in the same period of 2025, across 1,134 rounds, down from 1,838. By Tracxn's stage labels, early-stage funding rose 27% to $4.2 billion, late-stage funding held roughly flat at $5.4 billion, and seed funding fell 37% to $698 million.

Tracxn counted 18 rounds of $100 million or more. The largest were a $1 billion private equity deal in data centre company Nxtra, $600 million for AI infrastructure startup Neysa and $540 million for CRED. AI infrastructure was the most-funded business area at $1.2 billion. India added six unicorns in the period, compared with four a year earlier.

What investors are saying

Inc42 surveyed more than 85 institutional investors. Of those, 63% said Indian AI valuations had climbed beyond comfortable levels, and 32% expected a meaningful correction within the next 18 months. Only 12% thought current valuations were fully justified.

Exits are giving investors more options. Inc42 counted 22 mergers and acquisitions in the quarter, up from 13 a year earlier, and both Inc42 and Entrackr recorded six new-age tech IPO listings. For the companies queuing up next, see our startup news coverage.

Why it matters

The headline growth hides a tighter market. There are fewer deals, fewer active investors and less seed money, while capital pools in Series A and B companies and in AI, cleantech and deeptech. Seed-stage founders should plan for longer fundraises and closer questions on revenue. AI founders should be ready for valuation pushback if the correction many investors expect arrives.
